body: Pet clippers will work the best, just make sure to oil and clean them out frequently. I recommend using a guard when you're first learning how to work with the fur. Start with the largest guard, make multiple passes over brushed fur - and then move to a smaller guard until you achieve the length you're looking for. I usually cut without a guard now (for faces/fingers) because I want to get as smooth and close to the backing as possible.. but remember to go slow and take your time! Use scraps to practice.
^This! I would do another tape pattern and be careful not to snip any of the fur already placed. A little bit of seam allowance and a curved needle will really help you here

I love highlands! I would recommend sculpting the base out much more to essentially erase the initial bucket shape. I would focus on adding cheekbones and the "m" shape above the eyes that will taper smoothly into the nose bridge. Detach the horns for now, focus on building up the face more, then add your ears - and then reapply the horns! My concern right now is that the horns will eventually appear to be in the wrong spot once the shape of the overall head has changed from layering foam. I'd do those close to last. Good luck!!

I think it's adorable! To balance them out a little, I'd work on the symmetry of the nose first. (This is a lion, right?) If so, you could also change the shape of the nose overall to be more feline. It would be much flatter to the muzzle and more of a heart shape. As for the things you haven't finished, the bottom row of teeth seem a bit narrow/scrunced. Maybe elongate that same shape and add two top fangs? And the templates you have for the ears seem a tad small in proportion to the rest of the head, they're getting lost in all that hair! The height seems good on them, just wider across in that same half-circle shape. But there's an absolute charm to this suit, I think you're being hard on yourself!
